about: Real-world reference ranges GOKU compares the game against. These are TYPICAL published/engineering ranges for a class (not one specific person or car model). A value outside a range means 'look at this', not 'this is a bug'. Add exact models in `models` when you give me real specs.

basis.vehicle: typical automotive spec ranges per body class (general manufacturer data)
basis.human: typical adult anthropometry (standing height, limb/segment proportions)
basis.joints: typical human joint range of motion (knee/elbow flexion; no hyperextension)
basis.building: typical floor-to-floor heights (residential ~2.7-3.2 m, commercial up to ~3.6-4.2 m)
basis.ground: a standing or walking person always has one foot on the ground

human.note: legRatio = (thigh+shin bone lengths) / body height; armRatio = (upper-arm+forearm bone lengths) / height; shoulderRatio = shoulder-joint distance / height. Bone-length sums do not change when a limb is bent. Height is measured in idle pose.

joints.note: wrong way = knee/elbow bent while the joint sits on the wrong side of the hip-ankle / shoulder-wrist line

building.note: landmark value = whole model height / floors, so roofs, parapets and tanks are included (APPROX)

notMeasurableYet: face shape / eye spacing / nose-mouth proportions: face parts are not tagged in the character builder (needs Step 1: characters)
stairs, doors, windows, railings: the game has no interiors or stair/door data yet (a stair 'tower' is a plain box)
does a car LOOK like its real counterpart (grille, lights, body lines): needs real photos/blueprints + a person or vision AI to look
clothing clipping, skin/texture realism, brand-specific model dimensions (give me the model and I add its real specs to `models`)
muscle volume profile along limbs (thigh/calf taper) - needs a width-slice measure (next)
joint gaps / creases at knee, elbow, shoulder when bent (rigid skinning) - needs a close-up picture check
arm swing and weapon-hold pose (a weapon IK overrides the clips)
foot IK in motion (needs real input, moving hero)
vehicle behaviour while driving forward / reverse / turning (separate vehicle motion tool, next)

groundContact.note: height of the LOWEST foot/toe bone above the ground the character stands on (m). While standing/walking/chasing at least one foot is on the ground, so the lowest foot should sit within a few cm of it (ankle bone ~0.04-0.14 m). Above 0.2 m = floating, below -0.1 m = sunk into the ground. Jumping/falling/dead characters are skipped.

motion.basis: typical adult gait biomechanics, textbook ranges (ESTIMATE: not measured by us, not one specific person)

vehicleMotion.basis: typical road-vehicle dynamics, textbook ranges (ESTIMATE: not one specific model)
